title: Manipur Government Forms Enquiry Committee After Liquor Tragedy Claims 17 Lives; 4,500 Litres Seized
summary: Manipur has formed an Enquiry Committee into the suspected spurious liquor tragedy that claimed 17 lives. Around 4,500 litres have been seized, and samples sent to three laboratories for testing.
body:
Imphal, November 22, 2026: The Manipur Government has constituted an Enquiry Committee to investigate the deaths linked to the suspected spurious liquor tragedy in the state, which has claimed 17 lives, Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh announced on Sunday.

Addressing a press conference at the Durbar Hall of his Secretariat, the Chief Minister said the committee would thoroughly examine the incident, identify everyone involved and ensure that those found guilty are brought to justice at the earliest.

Government spokespersons Dr. Th. Radheshyam Singh and Dr. Sapam Ranjan Singh briefed the media on the latest developments in the case. The Chief Minister assured that the investigation would be taken to its logical conclusion and that all those responsible would be held accountable.

As part of the investigation, samples connected with the case have been sent to three laboratories for detailed examination: the National Food Laboratory in Kolkata, the Forensic Science Laboratory in Manipur and the State Public Health Laboratory. The analysis is expected to assist investigators in examining the suspected liquor and establishing relevant evidence.

The Chief Minister also disclosed that around 4,500 litres of liquor had been seized in connection with the case. The seizure forms part of the ongoing investigation into the suspected distribution and circulation of adulterated liquor.

Inspector General of Police Themthing Ngashangva, the Commissioner of Excise and the Director of Health were also present at the press conference, indicating the involvement of police, excise and health authorities in the government's response.

The tragedy has raised serious concerns over public safety and the circulation of potentially dangerous liquor in the state. With 17 reported deaths, the investigation will be crucial in establishing the circumstances surrounding the incident, identifying the sources of the liquor and determining accountability.

The government has assured the public that the enquiry will proceed and that those found responsible will face action in accordance with the law.
author: Mirror Lilong Desk
